findings.title: Command's interpreter is not in the image
findings.cause: container web cannot run /scripts/run.sh, though the file is there (key run.sh of ConfigMap scripts): the kernel reports "no such file or directory" for the interpreter named on the script's first line (#!), which image docker.io/library/busybox:1.37.0@sha256:a7dbc319b1438115a207e11930dc4bb3e643dcb3ec0bdd694bb36cd8fad289ec does not have; its log says: "exec /scripts/run.sh: no such file or directory"; Deployment web has 0 of 1 replicas ready

evidence.what: container web exited with code 255 (Error), restarted 8 times
last lines of container web's log (run that exited)
evidence.detail: exec /scripts/run.sh: no such file or directory

evidence.what: container web mounts volume scripts (ConfigMap scripts) at /scripts
the first line of run.sh names the interpreter
evidence.command: kubectl get configmap scripts -n kd-script-interpreter-missing -o jsonpath='{.data}'

findings.fix: Read the first line of run.sh in ConfigMap scripts. Name an interpreter the image has (#!/bin/sh where there is no bash), or use an image that has it; and save the file with Unix line endings, since a Windows line ending makes the kernel look for an interpreter whose name ends in a carriage return.
